technical_and_design_decisions: Use Hyperledger Fabric v1.0 architecture as the baseline for all development and documentation.
Implement the Node SDK using standard Node.js and gRPC libraries to interact with the blockchain.
Leverage the existing Lifecycle Chaincode (LCCC) and System Chaincode (SCC) frameworks to handle peer upgrades without data loss.
Split documentation into two distinct tracks: v0.6 for stable operational use and v1.0 for ongoing development updates.
Implement sanity checks at the transaction processing level to restrict invocations to LCCC or normal chaincodes only.
assumptions: One workday equals 8 hours of focused development effort.
The developer is already familiar with Hyperledger Fabric, Go, and Node.js.
Existing CI/CD pipelines and basic test frameworks are in place and do not require setup from scratch.
Gerrit references provided in the specification are accessible and provide the necessary context for implementation.
Visual aids and scripts refer to architectural diagrams and CLI demo scripts, not a full graphical user interface.
The Node SDK will cover basic interaction capabilities (connect, invoke, query) rather than a fully exhaustive enterprise SDK.

activities.activity_description: Create a quick start guide and improve navigation for new visitors to easily find what they need (U1).
Implement and document the new-channel configuration transaction, including fields and values, based on FAB-687 and Gerrit 1795 (U2).
Develop the ability to upgrade peers in case of protocol changes without data loss using LCCC and SCC (U3).
Fix ledger code and tests using old block structures and remove explicit dependency of ledger unit tests on MSP security (U4).
Create visual aids and demo scripts to explain and show the present architecture and behavior of Fabric v1.0 (U5).
Set up up-to-date documentation, directing users to v0.6 for stable platform and v1.0 for development documentation (U6).
Implement sanity checks to ensure that only LCCC or normal chaincodes can be invoked (U7).
Develop a Node SDK to allow developers to build applications with NodeJS to interact with the blockchain (U8).
